scope: Proposition 5.5 (Rational trace and contraction rules) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose E(Q)[2] ̸= 0. (i) For matching U, on the subtracted vector HU , t(g)t(u) = 0 (u split). The trace on split elements factors through the elementary extension of F supported on S ∪ U. For opposite U, on BU , every product of two traces is zero, and traces factor through the rational elementary extension supported there. (ii) If U ∪ {q} has the parity of the filter, its symbol is read at coefficient 1 by t(Frq) on HU for split q, and on BU for simple q. (iii) Fix p ∈ U and put g = Frq. Replacing g by gτp changes the symbol, additively in F2, by A (U/p) ∪ {q′ }  , Frq′ ∼ gϕp, (5.8) if p and q are not both simple. The label of q′ is required only away from the omitted primes and carries their product labels. The replacement uses the original source with level support S ∪ (U/p): the whole rational prime p is omitted, including both places over it if p splits in F. If both endpoints are simple, the change is zero. (iv) A split vertex with trivial label relative to the level with that vertex omitted has symbol zero.
